rows.note: This is the everyday all-purpose choice for calling someone mean or unkind, though it can also simply mean bad.

example.english: The way you treated that old person was really unkind.
example.traditional: 你咁樣對個老人家，真係好衰。
example.jyutping: nei5 gam3 joeng2 deoi3 go3 lou5 jan4 gaa1 zan1 hai6 hou2 seoi1

rows.note: Use this when the person seems cold, lacking sympathy, or unwilling to show kindness rather than merely unpleasant.

example.english: They saw how badly off the others were and still would not help; that was really unkind.
example.traditional: 佢見到人哋咁慘都唔肯幫手，真係冇人情味。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gin3 dou2 jan4 dei6 gam3 caam2 dou1 m4 hang2 bong1 sau2 zan1 hai6 mou5 jan4 cing4 mei6

rows.note: Use this specifically for the ungrateful slice of “unkind,” when someone fails to appreciate or repay kindness received.

example.english: They helped him so much before, but now he acts as if they do not exist; that is really unkind.
example.traditional: 人哋以前咁幫佢，而家佢竟然當人哋冇到，真係忘恩負義。
example.jyutping: jan4 dei6 ji5 cin4 gam3 bong1 keoi5 ji4 gaa1 keoi5 ging2 jin4 dong3 jan4 dei6 mou5 dou3 zan1 hai6 mong4 jan1 fu6 ji6
